nodes.name: Sol-gel synthesis of RuIrCaOx
nodes.procedure: Ru, Ir, Ca, and O elements were distributed evenly over the entire electrocatalyst via sol-gel synthesis method, resulting in a ternary RuIrCaOx oxide with shortened metal-oxygen bonds (Ru-O and Ir-O) compared to binary RuIrOx and benchmark RuO2 and IrO2.
nodes.source_text: By using the sol-gel synthesis method, Ru, Ir, Ca, and O elements were distributed evenly over the entire electrocatalyst... The Fourier transformed extended X-ray absorption fine structure (FT-EXAFS) spectroscopy of Ru K-edge and Ir L3-edge elucidate that the Ru-O bond of RuIrCaOx is much shorter than those of RuIrOx and RuO2, and Ir-O bond is slightly shorter compared to RuIrOx and IrO2.

nodes.name: Electrodeposition of AgOx nanoparticles
nodes.procedure: Silver oxide nanoparticles (AgOx-NP) were generated in-situ on conductive substrates (ITO or glass carbon) via cyclic voltammetry between 0.1 V and 1.6 V versus normal hydrogen electrode (NHE) in a HCO3-/CO2 system containing AgNO3. Formation of AgOx-NPs occurs via anodic electrodeposition of Ag+ at the potential region from +0.55 V to +0.75 V versus NHE. Upon further anodic scanning, a sharp OER catalytic current rises at about 1.28 V. The preparation of AgOx-NPs could also be achieved via electrodeposition at constant-potential electrolysis (CPE) at higher potentials (1.42 V vs NHE) showing higher growth and formation rates than lower CPE potentials (1.33 and 1.37 V vs NHE).
nodes.method: Electrodeposition via cyclic voltammetry and constant-potential electrolysis
nodes.source_text: A unique, in-situ generated silver oxide nanoparticle (AgOx-NP) has been synthesized... The AgOx-NPs were generated in-situ on conductive substrates (ITO or glass carbon) via cyclic voltammetry between 0.1 V and 1.6 V versus normal hydrogen electrode (NHE) in a HCO3-/CO2 system containing AgNO3.

nodes.name: Electrochemical activation of transition metal phosphides
nodes.procedure: Metallic phosphides (Co2P, CoP, and Ni2P nanoparticles) were used as pre-catalysts and underwent electrochemical activation in harsh alkaline solutions. The activation in harsh alkaline solution results in a 2-fold enhanced OER activity and affords 10 mA cm-2 with a significantly decreased overpotential of 100 mV, compared to direct electrochemical activation in neutral phosphate electrolyte.
nodes.source_text: Xie's group used a set of metallic phosphides, Co2P, CoP, and Ni2P nanoparticles (NPs), as representative pre-catalysts to demonstrate the advantages of electrochemical activation in harsh alkaline solutions. In contrast to the directly electrochemical activation in neutral phosphate electrolyte, the activation in harsh alkaline solution results in a 2-fold enhanced OER activity and affords 10 mA cm-2 with a significantly decreased overpotential of 100 mV.

nodes.name: Electrodeposition of Cu-Ci catalyst
nodes.procedure: Copper-based OER electrocatalyst (Cu-Ci) was prepared through simple electrolysis of inorganic Cu2+ salts within CO2-saturated (bi)carbonate solutions on various conductive substrates. In CO2-saturated, near-neutral NaHCO3 solution (0.1 M, pH ≈ 6.7), a stable OER current density of 0.35 mA cm-2 could be sustained for at least 3 h with adding 1.2×10-3 M Cu2+ at 1.55 V versus NHE. An amorphous solid film containing copper, oxygen, and carbon formed on the electrode during electrolysis in 1.0 M Na2CO3 solution, which is stable in non-buffered salt solutions.
nodes.source_text: Meyer and coworkers reported that the resulting material through simple electrolysis of inorganic Cu2+ salts within CO2-saturated (bi)carbonate solutions on various conductive substrates is catalytically active for OER in the near-neutral Ci electrolytes... In CO2-saturated, near-neutral NaHCO3 solution (0.1 M, pH ≈ 6.7), a stable OER current density of 0.35 mA cm-2 could be sustained for at least 3 h with adding 1.2×10-3 M Cu2+ at 1.55 V versus NHE.

nodes.name: Electrodeposition of Ni-Ci catalyst
nodes.procedure: Self-assembled Ni-based OER electrocatalyst (Ni-Ci) was prepared via electrolysis of Ni2+ in near-neutral bicarbonate solution with or without saturated CO2. The resulting Ni-Ci exhibits a nanoworm texture on the ITO substrate. The film is a mixture of Ni(OH)2 (Ni2+ species) and γ-NiOOH (Ni3+ species) with some NiO that transforms into hydroxide during the electrolysis course.
nodes.source_text: In 2014, de Groot's group developed a self-assembled Ni-based OER electrocatalyst (Ni-Ci) via electrolysis of Ni2+ in near-neutral bicarbonate solution with/without saturated CO2... An enlarged SEM image demonstrates the nanoworm texture of the Ni-Ci electrocatalyst on the ITO.

nodes.name: Electrodeposition of Co-Ci catalyst
nodes.procedure: Co-Ci catalyst was obtained via electrodeposition of Co2+ in bicarbonate electrolyte. The currents for both electrocatalyst deposition and OER increase linearly with the concentration of Co2+ in the aqueous NaHCO3 electrolyte. SEM images of the Co-Ci electrocatalysts reveal the surface morphology of small particle aggregates. The OER performance of Co-Ci is better than that of Co-Pi prepared by a similar method with phosphate instead.
nodes.source_text: In the same year, Joya and de Groot reported a slightly modified method to obtain a Co-Ci catalyst in bicarbonate electrolyte as well... Additionally, the currents for both electrocatalyst deposition and OER increase linearly with the concentration of Co2+ in the aqueous NaHCO3 electrolyte.

nodes.name: Electrodeposition of Fe-Ci catalyst
nodes.procedure: Fe-based electrocatalyst (Fe-Ci) was developed for highly efficient and stable OER via electrodeposition in a HCO3-/CO2 electrolyte containing 1×10-3 M Fe2+ ions. During controlled potential electrolysis at 1.3 V versus NHE, a stable current density of 4 mA cm-2 can be retained for at least 18 h.
nodes.source_text: Known as the most abundant transition metal, the Fe-based electrocatalyst (Fe-Ci) was developed for highly efficient and stable OER via electrodeposition in a HCO3-/CO2 electrolyte containing 1×10-3 M Fe2+ ions by Sun's group. During controlled potential electrolysis at 1.3 V versus NHE, a stable current density of 4 mA cm-2 can be retained for at least 18 h.

nodes.name: Galvanostatic oxidation of NiFe foam to form NiFe-HC
nodes.procedure: Nickel-iron hydroxide carbonate (NiFe-HC) was discovered by galvanostatic oxidation (at 250 mA cm-2) of a bimetallic Ni-Fe composite foam in 0.1 M KHCO3 solution at 85°C. Due to the OER on the NiFe foam accompanied with anodic etching, a porous, flower-like, and near-amorphous NiFe layer-double hydroxide (LDH) flakes was formed. The elemental mapping reveals an atomic ratio of Ni:Fe:C ≈ 15:1:3.4. The high concentration of C implies the intercalated carbonate anions into the NiFe-LDH layers.
nodes.source_text: Dai's group discovered a nickel-iron hydroxide carbonate (NiFe-HC) by galvanostatic oxidation (at 250 mA cm-2) of a bimetallic Ni-Fe composite foam in 0.1 M KHCO3 solution at 85°C. Due to the OER on the NiFe foam accompanied with anodic etching, a porous, flower-like, and near-amorphous NiFe layer-double hydroxide (LDH) flakes was formed.

nodes.name: Synthesis of Sr2GaCoO5 Brown-millerite oxide
nodes.procedure: Sr2GaCoO5 (SGC) was synthesized as a Brown-millerite structured oxide with ordered cation arrangement. The structure features GaO4 tetrahedra replacing CoO6 octahedra, lowering the Oh symmetry to D4h and breaking the degeneracy of both the t2g and eg orbitals. This structure stabilizes the intermediate state of low-spin (LS) Co3+ (t2g5eg1), which benefits the OER activity. The SGC maintains high crystallinity with lattice fringes extending to the surface after 100 CV cycles at neutral pH.
nodes.source_text: HAADF-STEM image of Sr2GaCoO5 (SGC). The right-side model illustrates the observed ordering of cations that matches the Brown-millerite structure... Due to the oxygen vacancy in SGC by GaO4 replacing, the Oh symmetry is lowered to D4h and has broken as well as the degeneracy of both the t2g and eg orbitals is broken.

nodes.source_text: The NiCoFeP electrocatalyst exhibits remarkable OER activity, achieving a current density of 10 mA cm^-2 at an overpotential of only 330 mV. The new electrocatalyst surpasses the mono- and bi-metal reference NiP and NiCoP as well as the leading noble metal oxide, IrO_2 and maintains the high activity for 100 h.

nodes.characterization_summary: Machine learning model developed for ultrafast covalency competition screening in spinel oxides with dataset of over 300 spinel oxides predicts Al₀.₅Mn₂.₅O₄ to exhibit relatively higher catalytic activity for OER, confirmed by subsequent electrochemical experiments.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Among various transition metal spinel oxides, Al₀.₅Mn₂.₅O₄ was predicted to exhibit a relatively higher catalytic activity for OER, which was further confirmed by the subsequent electrochemical experiments.

nodes.characterization_summary: Ambient pressure XPS reveals chemical and structural transformations of Co₃O₄/Co(OH)₂ into CoO(OH) as a function of applied anodic potentials, showing O 1s, Co 2p, and valence band spectral changes.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The simulation and multiplet fitting of O 1s, Co 2p, and valence band (VB) APXPS spectra discover that the chemical and structural transformations of Co₃O₄/Co(OH)₂ into CoO(OH) could be modeled as a function of the applied anodic potentials.

nodes.characterization_summary: Operando soft X-ray absorption spectroscopy of TM-Co-Pi films shows abundant Co³⁺ ions and low-lying O 2p conduction band edge indicating outstanding OER activities, with Mn dopant stabilizing Co³⁺ formation.
nodes.evidence_snippet: According to the Mn L-edges and the O K-edge, abundant Co³⁺ ions in the hybrid films and a low-lying O 2p conduction band (CB) edge indicate the outstanding OER activities.

nodes.characterization_summary: Operando resonant inelastic X-ray scattering of MnOₓ shows progressive increase of charge transfer from O 2p to Mn 3d with potentials over 1.75 V versus RHE, indicating enhanced Mn-O hybridization.
nodes.evidence_snippet: RIXS spectra of Mn L-edge suggest a progressive increase of charge transfer from O 2p to Mn 3d with potentials over 1.75 V versus RHE.

nodes.evidence_snippet: By using the sol-gel synthesis method, Ru, Ir, Ca, and O elements were distributed evenly over the entire electrocatalyst, as demonstrated by the energy dispersive spectroscopy (EDS) images.

nodes.characterization_summary: Fourier transformed extended X-ray absorption fine structure spectroscopy of Ru K-edge and Ir L₃-edge shows RuIrCaOₓ has much shorter Ru-O bonds than RuIrOₓ and RuO₂, and slightly shorter Ir-O bonds compared to RuIrOₓ and IrO₂.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The Fourier transformed extended X-ray absorption fine structure (FT-EXAFS) spectroscopy of Ru K-edge and Ir L₃-edge elucidate that the Ru-O bond of RuIrCaOₓ is much shorter than those of RuIrOₓ and RuO₂.

nodes.evidence_snippet: The coordination of Cu²⁺ in the high concentration of the buffer anions provides a proton acceptor and prevents the precipitation of Cu²⁺ as Cu(OH)₂ or CuCO₃ in neutral/weakly basic media, confirmed by the blue shift in ultraviolet-visible spectroscopy (UV-vis).

nodes.characterization_summary: Gas chromatography measurement shows production of 14 μmol of O₂ over 3 h electrolysis at 1.55 V versus NHE with Faradaic efficiency of approximately 96% for Cu²⁺-catalyzed OER in CO₂-saturated NaHCO₃ solution.

nodes.evidence_snippet: To probe the presence of CO₃²⁻, the time-of-flight secondary ion mass spectroscopy (TOF-SIMS) imaging at the surface and ≈ 30 nm depth was conducted. The m/z signals of 60, 44, 30, and 22 were detected not only at the surface, but also at ≈ 15 and ≈ 30 nm depth of the NiFe-LDH.
